solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drink breaks announced by a drunk?

indicators.note: something announced is spoken, and a drunk's slurred speech thickens every S into SH

blocks.note: to break is to snap, and the word slurred comes out with a thick SH at the start

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drinking break and makes an announcement while tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks' is SNAPS; a drunk says it as SHNAPS, which sounds like the liquor. The question mark flags the comic slurring.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong distilled spirit, often fruit-flavoured, from Germany and Scandinavia.

clue.text: Striking motion

blocks.note: first meaning: notable or remarkable
second meaning: a gesture made to convey a message

explanation.walkthrough: The pair reads like a single phrase about hitting out; the adjective sense of the answer, meaning outstanding, is the less familiar one.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means conspicuous or outstanding; as a noun it is a gesture used to communicate.

clue.text: Make Sacred Hearts to wear

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
to wear something, in informal British use, is to put up with or permit it

explanation.surface: Instructions to make Sacred Heart badges or emblems for people to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals suggest the Sacred Heart devotion, but 'Make Sacred' is the definition. In British slang 'I won't wear that' means 'I won't allow that'.
explanation.definitionFit: To hallow is to consecrate or bless something, setting it apart as holy.

clue.text: Close to all right-angled triangles have this

blocks.note: first meaning: beside or next to
second meaning, read as three words: every such triangle has a hypotenuse, its longest edge

explanation.surface: A geometry statement that nearly all right-angled triangles share some property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like a hint to take a final letter, but it is a definition; split the answer as A LONG SIDE for the triangle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something positioned beside another thing is next to it, near it, at its side.

clue.text: Gaze on drunken reps, certain why teens act the same?

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about unsteadily, so these letters lurch into a new order

blocks.note: to peer is to look intently
taken as written
certain means sure

explanation.surface: Watching tipsy sales reps leads someone to ask why teenagers behave identically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places the first piece before the rest. Reps (sales representatives) are a crossword favourite for anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenagers conform largely because of influence from friends their own age who push them to fit in.

clue.text: Doctor embracing strike with a strong spirit

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, wrapping your arms round someone, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
to rap is to hit sharply
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor hugging a striking worker, both of them fortified by strong spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like the link to the definition but it really adds A after the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian brandy distilled from grape pomace, notably potent.

clue.text: Bread yet not fully available

indicators.note: what is not fully there is only partly present, so the letters sit inside a longer stretch of the clue

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words, dropping the outer ones

explanation.surface: The loaves aren't completely on sale yet.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts after the first letter of 'Bread' and stops after the first letter of 'yet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prepared and at hand for use is on hand, accessible, there when required.

clue.text: Prior speaking of a cleric’s work

blocks.note: prior means earlier, gone by
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: A prior in a monastery talking about a priest's duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' poses as a monastic head, which fits the churchy surface, but it is the adjective meaning earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral care is a minister's spiritual guidance of the flock, the shepherding side of clergy duties.

clue.text: Some teachers supporting utter fools

indicators.note: in a down answer, what supports another thing lies underneath it, so this piece comes second

blocks.note: to utter a view is to air it
head teachers, the ones in charge of schools

explanation.surface: Certain teachers back complete idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' reads as an adjective, complete, but it is the verb meaning to voice.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is slang for a silly, empty-headed person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Irritated about work being hurried up?

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: galled means vexed or annoyed
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed that their job is being rushed through.
explanation.walkthrough: Up here means on horseback, as a rider is 'up', which the question mark signals; OP for opus is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse and rider at full speed in its fastest gait are rushing along mounted.

clue.text: Ruler of Cana escapes after being evacuated

indicators.note: an evacuated building is emptied of its contents, so each word keeps only its shell

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the Galilean town, its middle emptied out
the first and last letters, its middle emptied out
the first and last letters, its middle emptied out

explanation.surface: A ruler of the biblical town of Cana flees once the town is cleared of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a positional instruction, but it is the third word to be emptied, along with the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar became the title of Roman emperors, and so stands for any autocratic monarch.

clue.text: Like a small town career, it provides no competition

blocks.note: a one-horse town is a tiny, dull place
to career is to rush headlong

explanation.surface: A job in a sleepy little town offers nobody any rivalry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun about a job, but it is the verb for speeding along.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest with a certain winner, where one entrant is far ahead, is no real contest at all.

clue.text: Close to resuming after a day in between

indicators.note: after means following, so this piece is placed behind the others
the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday
its final letter

explanation.surface: Something nearly restarting after a gap of a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' sounds like the definition, near, but it takes the last letter; the definition is 'in between'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being surrounded by or situated amid things means being in the middle of them.

clue.text: Honest pay for modelling underwear

indicators.note: modelling is shaping material into a new form, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A model is getting fair wages for showing off lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modelling underwear' reads as a job description, but the participle is the anagram signal and 'underwear' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantyhose, chiefly American, are sheer tights worn on the legs and lower body, a type of hosiery.

clue.text: River drawn by travel writer

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece is set right next to another

blocks.note: to ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle
R is the map abbreviation for river
drawn, of a face, means gaunt and tired

explanation.surface: A river sketched by an author who writes about journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travel writer' looks like the definition, but 'travel' is a block. H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Rider Haggard was a Victorian novelist famous for African adventure stories such as She.

clue.text: Arranges things, as couples run out of sprouts

indicators.note: something out of a place has left it, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a seed that sprouts starts to grow
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone lays out vegetables in pairs after the Brussels sprouts are used up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sprouts' reads as the vegetable, but it is the verb, starts to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: To geminate is to double or arrange in pairs, from Latin gemini, twins.

clue.text: Leaders in trouble who often turned to lying

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so each word gives up its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the three words
to turn to someone is to face them

explanation.surface: Political leaders in difficulty who frequently resorted to telling lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned to lying' looks like one phrase meaning took up deceit; the break comes after 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-faced person is insincere and deceitful, saying one thing and meaning another.

clue.text: Time in ghastly refuges

indicators.note: in means inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: ghastly means hideous
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A spell spent in horrible shelters.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter goes in just before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideout is a hiding place, somewhere safe to shelter from pursuers.

clue.text: Hands seizing the result of some novel work?

definitions.text: Hands seizing the result of some novel work?

blocks.note: surface: workers or crew grabbing hold of something

blocks.clueFragment: the result of some novel work
blocks.note: setter's reading: hands that seize up after a long stint of writing fiction

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' suggests farmhands and 'seizing' suggests grabbing, but read it as hands seizing up in a painful spasm after penning a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the muscle spasm in the hand and fingers brought on by prolonged penmanship.

clue.text: Mail letter beginning role in romance

indicators.note: the letter at a word's beginning is its first, so just that one is taken
in means inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: amour is a love affair
its opening letter

explanation.surface: Posting a letter that starts someone's part in a love story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail letter' looks like posting something, but 'Mail' alone is the definition, meaning chain mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain mail is protective metal covering worn in battle, a kind of body armour.

clue.text: What Sudan’s first American vicar is up against

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
in a down answer, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the order runs backwards

blocks.note: its opening letter
US is short for the United States, so American
Rev is short for Reverend, a vicar's title

explanation.surface: Asking what the leading American clergyman in Sudan is struggling against.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up against' reads as a phrase meaning facing difficulty, but it splits: the reversal signal, then the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Versus is Latin for turned towards, used to mean opposed to, as in a match or lawsuit.

clue.text: French First Lady captivated by Irish poetry

indicators.note: someone captivated is held captive, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for French
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland
Eve is the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: The wife of the French president is charmed by poems from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French First Lady' looks like one person, the president's wife, but it splits into the abbreviation and the biblical first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Free verse is unrhymed poetry without a regular metre, a form of modern verse writing.

clue.text: Air failing to retain oxygen

indicators.note: to retain is to hold onto, so one piece keeps another inside it

blocks.note: a failing is a moral fault or vice
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Air that runs short of oxygen, as in a stuffy room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' is the verb here, to express an opinion, not the gas the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a grievance is to express it out loud, to give it utterance.

clue.text: Sauce bottle

blocks.note: first meaning: impudence or cheek
second meaning: British slang for courage

explanation.walkthrough: The pair suggests a ketchup container; both words are British informal terms, sauce for cheek and bottle for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both brazen impudence and steady courage, matching the two slang senses.

clue.text: Relative states during change

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: change is loose coins
US stands for the United States

explanation.surface: A claim that relative conditions hold while things alter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative' sounds like an adjective, comparative, but it is the noun, a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a family member, the child of one's aunt or uncle.

clue.text: Nit-picking about proper evidence of liabilities

blocks.note: c is short for circa, about
apt means fitting or proper
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Someone fussing over correct documentation of debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container signal, but here it simply gives circa's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Captious describes someone fault-finding and carping, inclined to raise trivial objections.

clue.text: Editor-in-chief uses these in print runs

blocks.note: first meaning: the short horizontal marks joining the words of that title
second meaning: hurries, sprints

explanation.walkthrough: 'Print runs' looks like a publishing term, but the split is after 'print'; the clue's own title displays the marks it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Short horizontal punctuation strokes link words, and to sprint is a verb with the same spelling.

clue.text: Worried about more than just a trifle

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: worried means anxious or tense

explanation.surface: Someone anxious over something more serious than a minor matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifle' seems to mean a small matter, but it is the layered British pudding of sponge, custard and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle is one example of a sweet course, so puddings in general cover more than it.
